description: We are an engineering team specializing in computer vision, deep learning, and predictive data systems, focused on modeling and mitigating hazards in mission-critical environments. Here, we will quantify flame propagation and material flammability to support safer design standards for pressurized orbital and planetary habitats.
summary:
Ember Atlas is an interactive, superintelligence-powered research workspace that synthesizes decades of NASA microgravity combustion research from the Physical Sciences Informatics repository.

In microgravity, the absence of buoyancy causes fires to burn as quiet, spherical blue flames that sustain invisible, low-temperature cool flame combustion. This challenge is urgent for the Artemis lunar program, where habitats and pressurized rovers will operate in high-oxygen environments of 30% to 34% oxygen at 10.2 psi, making standard materials drastically more flammable.

To solve the challenge of navigating massive, fragmented NASA flight data, Ember Atlas organizes 19 flight investigations across Prevention, Detection, and Suppression. It features an interactive microgravity droplet combustion simulator, an inspectable data explorer with 37 source-checked experimental runs across 10 core flight studies, multi-study comparative matrices, and a citation-grounded Super Intelligence assistant powered by Google Gemini.

Ember Atlas bridges raw spaceflight data and operational aerospace engineering, helping mission architects design safer lunar outposts, spacecraft ventilation loops, and long-duration Mars transit vehicles, while translating space discoveries into terrestrial firefighting and industrial safety technologies.
details:
1. The Challenge It Answers

Fire is one of the most lethal hazards in human space exploration. In microgravity, the absence of buoyant convection eliminates rising hot gases; flickering teardrop flames are replaced by spherical, diffusion-controlled blue flames that burn quietly and are difficult to detect and suppress.

This challenge is urgent: to facilitate frequent spacesuit EVAs on the Moon, the planned Artemis Moon Base and pressurized rovers will operate in an exploration atmosphere with elevated oxygen (≥30% O₂) and reduced pressure (10.2 psi or less). This represents an over 40% increase in oxygen concentration compared to Earth's atmosphere, making materials drastically more flammable.

While NASA has accumulated a trove of experimental data from flight investigations aboard the ISS (CIR, MSG) and uncrewed Cygnus spacecraft (Saffire), the sheer volume of heterogeneous files in the Physical Science Informatics (PSI) database makes them difficult to discover, compare, and translate into fire safety engineering standards. Ember Atlas solves this by turning raw, dispersed data into an intuitive, intelligence-driven research workspace.

2. How It Works

Ember Atlas combines rigorous data curation with a grounded Super Intelligence (SI) reasoning architecture:

• Evidence Discovery & Safety Ranking: Indexes 22 NASA microgravity combustion investigations across solid fuels, liquid droplets, gaseous flames, and aerosols. Studies are ranked on an objective safety relevance scale prioritizing human habitable environments.

• Grounded Super Intelligence (SI) Cascade: Powered by an intelligent multi-model cascade orchestrator. For deep reasoning and multi-study synthesis, it leverages Gemma 4 31B (14.4K RPD); for instant research chat and query assistance, it utilizes Gemini 3.5 & 3.1 Flash Lite. The SI operates under strict scientific boundaries: it answers only from verified investigation records, clearly distinguishes hypotheses from observed flight measurements, and cites exact investigation IDs (e.g., [PSI-69], [PSI-25], [PSI-98], [PSI-102]).

• Interactive Experimental Data Explorer: Features flight-run data tables (droplet burn times, initial and extinction diameters, chamber pressures, flow velocities) with dynamic Recharts metric visualizers, color-coded by test ending (Extinction vs. Disruption), with instant CSV/JSON exports.

• Side-by-Side Comparative Matrix: Contrasts up to three investigations simultaneously across 8 scientific parameters, highlighting hardware differences (CIR/MDCA vs. MSG flow ducts) and complementary findings.

• Exploration Scenarios & Terrestrial Spin-offs: Dedicated evaluation modules for Lunar 30%+ O₂ flammability, spacecraft ventilation-driven flame spread, Mars regolith dust vs. smoke detection (SAME/DAFT), and Earth spin-offs (fine-water-mist extinguishers, firefighter SCBA gear).

3. Scientific Integrity & Evidence Boundaries

Ember Atlas enforces strict scientific transparency:

• Microgravity (0g) ≠ Partial Gravity (1/6g Moon or 3/8g Mars): The PSI database currently contains zero sustained partial-gravity combustion data. Ember Atlas explicitly tags this boundary so researchers do not mistakenly extrapolate 0g microgravity data to lunar or Martian gravity without dedicated partial-gravity flight testing (such as the planned LUCI and FM2 investigations).

4. What We’d Build Next

• Ingestion of Full Sensor Time-Series & Schlieren Imagery: Expanding the numerical tables to include raw thermocouple wave curves, radiometer heat flux logs, and high-speed camera footage archives from PSI.

• Physics-Informed Flammability Modeling (PINNs): Integrating physics-informed neural network models trained on PSI flammability limits to predict solid material burn rates under custom O₂/pressure/flow mixtures.

• Partial-Gravity Integration: Ingesting upcoming data from the Lunar-g Combustion Investigation (LUCI) and Flammability of Materials on the Moon (FM2) as they fly.

• Habitat Edge PWA: Building an offline, lightweight progressive web application for deployment on isolated space habitat and rover local networks.
